title: नारीवादी दृष्टिकोणले ‘शाकुन्तल’ महाकाव्यको अध्ययन
nepali: भागिरथको गङ्गाझै नेपाली साहित्य धरतीमाअवतरण गरेको ‘शाकुन्तल’ महाकवि लक्ष्मीप्रसाद देवकोटाको अद्वितीय महाकाव्य हो । यसमा देवकोटाले पितृसत्तावाट पीडित नारी पात्रका रुपमा मेनका शकुन्तलालाई प्रस्तुत गरेका छन् भने पितृसत्ताको मूल्य अनुसरण गर्ने नारी पात्रका रुपमा गौतमीलाई प्रस्तुत गरेका छन् । यस महाकाव्यमा प्रयुक्त नारी पात्रका भूमिका कार्य व्यापार आदिद्वारा कवि तत्कालीन नेपाली समाजमा नारीहरुको अवस्था कस्तो थियो भनी देखाउन चाहन्छन् । नारीप्रति सहानुभूति राख्ने र नारी मैत्री मानिने देवकोटाद्वारा लेखिएको नारीकै नामसँग सम्बन्धित शीर्षक भएको यस महाकाव्यको नारीवादी दृष्टिले अध्ययन गर्नु उचित ठानी ‘नारीवादी दृष्टिले शाकुन्तल महाकाव्यको अध्ययन’ शीर्षक अनुसन्धानात्मक लेख तयार गरिएको छ । यस महाकाव्यको नारीवादी दृष्टिकोणवाट अध्ययन विश्लेषण गर्दा गुणात्मक अनुसन्धान ढाँचामा वर्णनात्मक र विश्लेषणात्मक विधिको उपयोग गरिएको छ । प्राथमिक र द्वितीयक श्रोतवाट सामग्री संकलन र त्यसको गहन अध्ययन गरी त्यसको गुणात्मक विश्लेषण गरिएको छ । आफ्नो यस महाकाव्यलाई ज्ञान, चातुरी, प्रेम र विलास सिक्ने पाठशाला मानेका देवकोटाले यसमा तत्कालीन नेपाली समाजको समग्र पक्षको चित्र हाम्रा सामु प्रस्तुत गरेका छन् । यस अध्ययनले शाकुन्तलभित्रको समाजका नारीहरुको अवस्थाका बारेमा उनीहरुमाथि पितृसत्ताद्वारा गरिएको दमन तथा त्यसको प्रतिरोधमा उठेका तरङ्गहरु बारे जानकारी गराउनुका साथै देवकोटाले नारीप्रतिको दृष्टिकोणको बारेमा जान्न चाहने जिज्ञासुको जिज्ञासा शान्त पार्न मद्दत गर्नेछ ।
american_english: Descending upon the realm of Nepali literature like Bhagiratha's Ganges, 'Shakuntal' is an unparalleled epic by the great poet Laxmi Prasad Devkota. In it, Devkota presents Menaka and Shakuntala as female characters victimized by patriarchy, whereas he presents Gautami as a female character who follows patriarchal values. Through the roles, actions, and conduct of the female characters employed in this epic, the poet seeks to show what the condition of women was like in contemporary Nepali society. Considering it appropriate to study this epic from a feminist perspective—written by Devkota, who sympathized with women and was regarded as woman-friendly, and bearing a title associated with a woman's name—the research article titled 'A Study of the Epic Shakuntal from a Feminist Perspective' was prepared. In studying and analyzing this epic from a feminist perspective, descriptive and analytical methods were utilized within a qualitative research design. Materials were collected from primary and secondary sources, studied in depth, and analyzed qualitatively. Devkota, who regarded this epic of his as a school for learning knowledge, wit, love, and indulgence, has presented before us a portrait of all facets of contemporary Nepali society. This study will provide insight into the condition of women in the society within Shakuntal, the oppression inflicted on them by patriarchy, and the ripples of resistance that arose, while helping satisfy the curiosity of seekers wanting to understand Devkota's outlook toward women.

informal_english: Dropping onto the scene of Nepali literature like Bhagiratha's Ganges, 'Shakuntal' is an absolute masterpiece of an epic by the great poet Laxmi Prasad Devkota. In it, Devkota shows Menaka and Shakuntala as female characters suffering under patriarchy, while showing Gautami as a woman who just sticks to patriarchal values. Through the roles, actions, and everyday affairs of the women in this epic, the poet wants to show us what things were really like for women in Nepali society back then. Thinking it made total sense to study this epic through a feminist lens—written by Devkota, who had real sympathy for women and was seen as pro-women, plus carrying a title named after a woman—the research paper titled 'A Study of the Epic Shakuntal from a Feminist Perspective' was put together. In studying and unpacking this epic from a feminist perspective, descriptive and analytical methods were used within a qualitative research design. Material was collected from primary and secondary sources, studied deeply, and analysed qualitatively. Devkota, who saw this epic of his as a proper school for learning knowledge, wit, love, and pleasure, laid out a full picture of every side of contemporary Nepali society right before us. This study sheds light on the situation of women in the society inside Shakuntal, the oppression dumped on them by patriarchy, and the waves of resistance that kicked up, while helping satisfy the curiosity of anyone keen to understand Devkota's views on women.
